definitions.gloss: one-upmanship; asserting social dominance; showing off superiority
definitions.explanation: The behavior of trying to establish oneself as superior to others in conversation or social situations, often through subtle boasting, name-dropping, or belittling others' achievements. A modern buzzword in Japanese social commentary.

examples.japanese: ⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧マウンティングだ⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
SNS⟦で→で：00502_de⟧マウンティング⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: There are a lot of people who try to one-up others on social media.

examples.japanese: ⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{成績|せいせき}→成績：03379_seiseki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{自慢|じまん}→自慢：03278_jiman⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦ただ→ただ：01613_tada⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧マウンティング⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧しか⟦{聞|き}こえない→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧。
examples.english: Bragging about your child's grades just sounds like one-upmanship.

notes:
Originally from animal behavior terminology (mounting to establish dominance), this loanword gained wide currency in Japanese from around 2015 as a buzzword describing competitive social behavior among humans. It is now commonly used in casual conversation, social media, and pop psychology.

The abbreviated form ⟦マウント→マウント：05983_maunto⟧ is also very common, especially in the phrase ⟦マウントを{取|と}る→マウントを取る：23480_mauntowotoru⟧ (to assert dominance).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- マウンティング⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to engage in one-upmanship
- ⟦マウントを{取|と}る→マウントを取る：23480_mauntowotoru⟧: to assert dominance, to one-up someone
- マウンティング⟦{女子|じょし}→女子：03350_joshi⟧: women who one-up each other
- ⟦{無意識|むいしき}→無意識：05813_muishiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧マウンティング: unconscious one-upmanship

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{自慢|じまん}→自慢：03278_jiman⟧: boasting — straightforward bragging, while マウンティング implies a competitive dynamic
- ⟦マウント→マウント：05983_maunto⟧: mount — shortened form used in the same way
- ⟦{見栄|みえ}を{張|は}る→見栄を張る：15322_miewoharu⟧: to put on airs — trying to look better than one is, but without the competitive element
